title: Not by reputation
hook: you can't be a philosopher by reputation; just live by nature (Meditations 8.1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: no frenzy, the last day lived calm, awake and real. Your line was quits their job by noon. Did you drop an act, even once? Day five hundred ninety-six.

An emperor sits alone with a notebook he writes to himself. Nobody is watching. He could put down anything he likes about who he is. Instead he writes a hard sentence: he is far from being a philosopher, and it's plain to others and plain to himself. No excuses, no softening. That's how book eight of the Meditations begins. Not with a triumph. With an honest confession, and then a way forward.
screen: `AN EMPEROR'S NOTEBOOK.` → `FAR FROM IT, AND HE SAYS SO.` → `BOOK EIGHT OPENS.`

segments.voice: First, the confession. In Meditations eight, one, Marcus says this thought helps against vanity: you can't claim to have lived your whole life, or even your adult life, as a philosopher. It's plain to many people, and to yourself, that you're far from it. Your position, he says, works against it. He doesn't soften it. Second, the trap. When you realize you're not what you'd like to be called, there's a temptation. Fix the reputation. Look more philosophical. Talk the part. Marcus closes that door. He says throw away the question of how you'll seem to others. Third, the way forward. Instead, he says, be content to live whatever remains of your life as your nature wants. And where is living well found? In doing what human nature asks. How do you do that? By holding principles from which your actions grow. So he moves the whole question from the label to the practice. Fourth, why it fits this book. On this path, book eight is about one action at a time, and this is its opening move. You can't become wise by being called wise. You can't fix a reputation by working on the reputation. You can only do the next thing well, quietly, again and again. And Marcus leaves room for it. Whatever remains, he says. Not the whole life. The rest of it. That's enough to work with.
screen: `I HAVEN'T LIVED AS A PHILOSOPHER.` · `DROP HOW YOU'LL SEEM.` · `LIVE AS YOUR NATURE ASKS.` · `WHATEVER REMAINS IS ENOUGH.` · then, large: `NOT BY REPUTATION.`

segments.voice: Sit, and breathe. Is there a label you'd like to wear? A good parent, a spiritual person, a hard worker, a kind friend. Notice how much effort goes into seeming that way. Let the label go for the length of this sit. Underneath it, find one small action that the label points to. Something you could do today that nobody would see. Picture doing it. That's the whole thing. The bell holds the time.
Marcus, who admitted he was far from a philosopher, and turned from the label to living by nature for whatever remained of his life. Today's word.
Your line: whatever remains of your life. Today, do one quiet good that nobody will ever connect to you. Let it be enough. Day five hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: Readers of Marcus often take 8.1 as permission to stop worrying about whether they look wise or spiritual, and to put their effort into small actions that follow from their principles.

original.note: Greek: opinion, reputation, how one seems to others.

trapdoor: what you thought: be humble about your achievements.
what it means: stop managing the label, and put everything into living by your principles for whatever time remains.
what a scholar hears: doxa covers both 'opinion' and 'reputation,' so for a Stoic, chasing a good name means living by other people's opinions.

notes: Meditations 8.1 paraphrased: against vainglory, you can't have lived your whole life, or from youth, as a philosopher; it's plain to many and to yourself you're far from philosophy; your plan of life opposes it; throw away how you'll seem; live the rest as nature wills; living well is in doing what man's nature requires, through principles from which come impulses and actions. Confirm.
'Philosopher-king' is a later label (from Plato's Republic, applied to Marcus by later writers); the hook presents it as how he's remembered. Confirm framing.
Confirm whether 8.1 uses doxa; the original game presents doxa as the general Greek word for reputation.
